title: A las doce en punto
desc: Arriving on time, and being put to work for two hours
setting: The invitation said twelve, it is twelve, and doña Carmen is in the patio with a broom and wet hair.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¡Ideay! ¿Ya vinieron? Si todavía no hay nada listo.
steps.en: Ideay! You are here already? There is nothing ready yet.

options.es: Llegamos temprano, doña. Póngame a hacer algo.
options.en: We came early, doña. Put me to work.
options.feedback: You are two hours early by local reckoning and there is only one way out of that: pick up a chair and start carrying.

options.es: La invitación decía a las doce.
options.feedback: It did, and twelve meant about two. Producing the evidence is the most foreign thing you could do standing in her patio.

options.en: Sorry, doña. Shall we come back later?
options.feedback: You will not be allowed to leave. Staying and helping is what happens next either way.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ay, mijo, agarrá esas sillas y ponelas alrededor.
steps.en: Oh, love, grab those chairs and put them round.

options.en: Right then. How many shall I put out?
options.feedback: Punctuality has a price here and this is it. Two hours of work, and by the end you know where everything in her kitchen lives.
Fine. You will put out the wrong number and carry them twice.

options.es: Lucía me dijo que era muy temprano.
options.en: Lucía told me it was too early.
options.feedback: She did, three times. Saying so now in front of everybody helps nobody, least of all you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: El primer invitado llega a la una y media, vas a ver.
steps.en: The first guest will arrive at half past one, you will see.

options.es: Entonces la hora nica es la de verdad y la otra es la escrita.
options.en: So the real time is the Nica one and the other is the written one.
options.feedback: That is it exactly. Nobody is being rude and nobody is late, because everybody except you is reading the same clock.
You have, at the cost of two hours of chairs.

options.es: Eso es una falta de respeto con usted.
options.feedback: She does not think so and she would have been horrified if they had turned up at twelve, because nothing was ready.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Así es aquí, mijo. Pero ya sabés: para la otra, venite a la una.
steps.en: That is how it is here, love. But now you know: next time, come at one.

options.es: A la una y media, mejor. Con hambre.
options.feedback: You went one better than she did, which is the joke she was fishing for. Arriving hungry is the other half of getting this right.
Agreed. She gave you the number, and by now you can work out the real one yourself.

options.en: I prefer to be on time.
options.feedback: You have just spent two hours carrying chairs for preferring to be on time. The lesson was free and you have refused it.
